outcome: blood glucose control (fasting, 1-hour, 2-hour postprandial glucose levels)
self-management ability (diabetes knowledge, behaviors, attitude, social support)
cohort: The study included 106 high-risk pregnant women diagnosed with Gestational Diabetes Mellitus (GDM), with 54 receiving the intervention and 52 receiving routine care.
finding: The risk perception-based nursing model significantly improved blood glucose control, self-management, and psychological adjustment, leading to lower rates of premature rupture of membranes, macrosomia, and neonatal hypoglycemia in high-risk GDM pregnant women.
mod_finding: The study found no significant difference in the cesarean section rate between the risk perception-based nursing model group and the routine care group.
birth_weight: Macrosomia was measured as an outcome for the newborns.
gest_age: Outcomes were assessed at 37 weeks of gestation, and preterm birth rate was measured as an outcome.
